blog_summary: The blog post discusses the paper 'Value Iteration Networks' by Tamar et al., which won a best paper award at NIPS 2016. The author, Adrian Colyer, highlights two key challenges in reinforcement learning addressed by the paper: incorporating longer-range planning into learned strategies and improving transfer learning between problems. The breakthrough insight is embedding a differentiable value iteration (VI) planning component within a neural network architecture, allowing the network to learn planning parameters via backpropagation. The VI algorithm, traditionally used in Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), is encoded as a convolutional neural network (CNN), making it differentiable. The resulting Value Iteration Networks (VINs) demonstrate better generalization to new grid-world scenarios compared to standard CNN-based reinforcement learning models. The post also notes the versatility of VINs, showing successful applications in Mars Rover navigation, physical simulation planning, and web navigation tasks. The author praises the elegance of the approach, where the network autonomously learns to use the planning machinery effectively.
paper_abstract: We introduce the value iteration network (VIN): a fully differentiable neural network with a ‘planning module’ embedded within. VINs can learn to plan, and are suitable for predicting outcomes that involve planning-based reasoning, such as policies for reinforcement learning. Key to our approach is a novel differentiable approximation of the value-iteration algorithm, which can be represented as a convolutional neural network, and trained end-to-end using standard backpropagation. We evaluate VIN based policies on discrete and continuous path-planning domains, and on a natural-language based search task. We show that by learning an explicit planning computation, VIN policies generalize better to new, unseen domains.
